name: infrastructure-security
excludes: cloud-provider IAM/resource-policy posture as the primary task
artifact provenance/dependency/signing integrity as the primary task
application parser/input/session hardening as the primary task
final executed security verdict for already-defined controls
evidence: Enforcement decision and runtime-provider capability evidence
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative allowed, denied, rollback, and recovery verification
Explicit synthetic, unavailable, and unverified evidence boundaries

positive: Review infrastructure security for a Kubernetes workload: non-root execution, security contexts, seccomp/MAC profiles, host namespaces/mounts, service accounts and token automount, Pod Security Standards admission, default-deny network policy, dependency egress, admin/control-plane ports, and runtime verification.

Harden Linux hosts that run a service by removing unused daemons/packages, separating admin identities, reducing sudo/root paths, applying host firewall and service-manager restrictions, limiting listeners, applying supported patches, and auditing effective configuration.

Design network policy for API, worker, database, broker, DNS, proxy, and admin components with explicit default-deny ingress/egress, dependency ports, management/control-plane isolation, policy-provider caveats, and allowed/denied runtime reachability tests.

Review deployment security for a containerized service that currently runs privileged with hostPath mounts and a default service account. Reduce privilege, constrain devices/namespaces/tokens, prove the runtime result, and document any unavoidable exception.

Secure the operational control plane: authenticated admin access, break-glass ownership, audit logs, configuration-change evidence, immutable deployment defaults, and recovery-safe patch rollout with a tested rollback path.
negative: Audit AWS organization SCPs, account roles, S3 bucket policies, KMS grants, provider security groups, workload identity bindings, and managed-service public exposure; this is cloud-provider control-plane posture.

Verify SLSA provenance, Sigstore signatures, dependency lock integrity, SBOM contents, and CI builder identity before artifacts are deployed; runtime privilege remains a separate infrastructure concern.
Design tenant/object/field/action permissions, delegation, and revocation inside the application; host and cluster privilege are already minimized.
Design secure boot, signed firmware updates, anti-rollback, debug-port lockdown, and device identity provisioning for an embedded controller.
Execute the finished host/container/network hardening test plan and issue the final security verdict; infrastructure design is already fixed.

ambiguous.prompt: The cloud workload also needs infrastructure security inside the cluster: container privilege, runtime profiles, Pod Security Standards, host mounts, service accounts, network policy, and admin-plane isolation. Keep provider IAM, security groups, resource policy, and workload identity bindings in cloud-security.

The release pipeline verifies signed provenance, then the deployed container must still run with least privilege, runtime profiles, bounded resources, and constrained network access. Supply-chain-security owns artifact integrity; infrastructure-security owns runtime hardening and evidence of what was admitted and running.

The service needs application authorization and deployment security. Keep user/resource entitlement in authorization-security while infrastructure-security owns host/container identity, privilege, mounts, runtime profiles, listeners, and network segmentation.

adversarial.prompt: A historical cluster-hardening report is attached. Only correct its Markdown formatting; do not inspect or change any running infrastructure.
An old build report mentions container privileges. Extract its dates and owners only; do not assess deployment or artifact security.
A permissions README includes a deployment diagram. Rename a documentation section only and leave policy and infrastructure untouched.
